answer: Whether agents trade quartz, map tundra routes, or forecast a zephyr, a marketplace can allocate access to paid jobs in proportion to tokens locked in escrow, with the same lock period for every account. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand identities earns the same total job quota as staking them under one identity. To capture more work, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens, tying up capital and sacrificing its use elsewhere.
